text: A Protocol Specification MUST possess one stable specification identity and MUST identify its specification version.

scope: Every completed Privacy Engine Protocol Specification
text: A completed Protocol Specification MUST identify exactly one published Privacy Engine protocol generation from which it derives.
A Protocol Specification MUST preserve the semantics and obligations of the published protocol generation from which it derives.

scope: Every completed Privacy Engine Protocol Specification
text: A completed Protocol Specification MUST contain the complete implementation-facing normative composition required to implement its identified published protocol generation without dependence on hidden repository context.
An incomplete cumulative Protocol Specification MUST NOT claim completeness, final publication status, or suitability as the complete conformance basis.

scope: Every Privacy Engine Protocol Specification and every interpretation of it
text: A Protocol Specification MUST NOT be treated as independent protocol authority or as authority to modify its source protocol generation.
A cumulative Protocol Specification MUST state its composition status, composed section families, deferred section families, and current completeness boundary.

scope: Every semantic requirement composed into the Protocol Specification
text: Each semantic requirement MUST possess exactly one authoritative normative home within the Protocol Specification, excluding every supporting reference from authoritative-home status.

The Protocol Specification MUST establish the downstream derivation rule requiring the implementation profile to identify the Protocol Specification and published Protocol Generation from which its applicable obligations derive.
The Privacy Engine Protocol MUST be defined independently of any particular implementation, application, deployment, transport, storage system, or execution environment.

scope: Every published Privacy Engine protocol generation
text: A published protocol generation MUST declare the complete bounded protocol scope represented by that generation.
Each protocol invariant MUST remain owned by the published protocol generation in which it is defined.

scope: Every downstream specification, profile, implementation, application, assessment, and certification artifact
text: A downstream artifact MUST NOT redefine, weaken, strengthen, omit, or silently reinterpret an applicable protocol invariant.

scope: Every claim of complete protocol realization
text: A claim of complete protocol realization MUST account for every applicable invariant and normative requirement of the identified published protocol generation.

scope: Every application and implementation using the Privacy Engine Protocol
text: Application-defined meaning and implementation-defined mechanism MUST NOT be represented as protocol-defined meaning unless the identified published protocol generation explicitly defines it.

scope: Every statement in the Protocol Specification
text: Every specification statement MUST be classifiable as normative or informative.
A requirement using `MUST` MUST be interpreted as mandatory throughout its declared applicability scope.
A requirement using `MUST NOT` MUST be interpreted as prohibiting the stated behavior throughout its declared applicability scope.
A requirement using `SHOULD` MUST be interpreted as recommended; deviation MUST be bounded, understood, and justified without violating any mandatory requirement.
A requirement using `SHOULD NOT` MUST be interpreted as discouraged; contrary behavior MUST be bounded, understood, and justified without violating any mandatory requirement.
A requirement using `MAY` MUST be interpreted as permitting, but not requiring, the stated behavior.
Implementation-defined behavior MUST be explicitly permitted, bounded by the applicable protocol requirements, and documented by the implementation.
Every normative requirement MUST declare a bounded applicability rule identifying the subjects and conditions to which it applies.

scope: Every interpretation of a normative requirement
text: A normative requirement MUST be interpreted using its identifier, requirement text, defined terminology, applicability rule, authoritative section, and applicable cross-references as one coherent requirement.

scope: Every supporting cross-reference and informative statement
text: A supporting cross-reference or informative statement MUST NOT independently create, modify, complete, weaken, strengthen, conceal, or relocate a normative obligation.
Every normative requirement MUST possess exactly one stable identifier in the form `PE-<SEMANTIC-FAMILY>-<NNN>`, and that identifier MUST denote exactly one semantic requirement.
A requirement identifier MUST NOT be changed because of editorial reordering and MUST NOT be silently reused for a different semantic requirement.
Every normative requirement MUST record its requirement family, strength, applicability, authoritative section, and supporting source traceability.
Every statement intended to impose an obligation MUST be expressed as a stable identified normative requirement rather than apparently mandatory prose.
A Protocol Generation MUST possess one unique and stable generation identity.
A Protocol Generation MUST contain one bounded and complete protocol semantic state.

scope: Every incomplete protocol fragment or partial change
text: An incomplete protocol fragment or partial change MUST NOT be represented as a complete Protocol Generation.
A Protocol Generation MUST retain the same identity through publication, coexistence, deprecation, migration, and retirement.
A Protocol Publication MUST identify exactly one complete Protocol Generation as its publication subject.
A Protocol Publication MUST identify the complete published material, generation identity, publication identity, and publication version required to distinguish its result.

scope: Every incomplete or ambiguous publication occurrence
text: An incomplete or ambiguously identified publication MUST NOT establish a Published Protocol.

A Protocol Publication MUST NOT be interpreted as Protocol Succession, Protocol Lineage membership, compatibility, deprecation, migration, or retirement unless those relationships are separately and explicitly established.
A Published Protocol MUST identify exactly one Protocol Generation and exactly one complete publication of that generation.
A Published Protocol MUST possess a stable identity distinct from the identity of its Protocol Generation and its Protocol Publication.
A Published Protocol MUST NOT be silently replaced, partially rewritten, or reinterpreted as a different generation.

scope: Every published Privacy Engine protocol generation
text: Each published Privacy Engine protocol generation MUST remain the protocol authority for its own identified semantics and obligations throughout its recorded lifecycle.
A Protocol Publication claiming completeness MUST contain or unambiguously bind every component required to reconstruct the complete published generation.
A Published Protocol MUST remain immutable after publication.

scope: Every correction, clarification, or replacement affecting published material
text: A correction, clarification, or replacement affecting published material MUST be separately identified and MUST preserve the identity and historical content of the earlier Published Protocol.
An incomplete publication MUST NOT be used as the authoritative representation of a complete Protocol Generation.
An implementation MUST identify exactly which published Protocol Generation it targets.
A conformance determination MUST identify the implementation, implementation profile, Protocol Specification, and published Protocol Generation against which conformance is assessed.
A certification MUST identify the conformance basis and published Protocol Generation to which the certification applies.

scope: Every downstream implementation or assessment artifact
text: A downstream implementation, profile, conformance determination, or certification MUST NOT modify the identity, semantics, obligations, lifecycle, or authority of its referenced published Protocol Generation.
A Protocol Succession relationship MUST identify exactly one predecessor Protocol Generation and one distinct successor Protocol Generation.
A successor Protocol Generation MUST possess an identity distinct from every predecessor generation.
Protocol Succession MUST preserve the identity, published content, lifecycle record, and historical truth of the predecessor generation.
Protocol Succession MUST NOT mutate, rename, merge, delete, or retroactively reinterpret its predecessor generation.
Publication of a generation MUST NOT by itself establish succession from any other generation.
A Protocol Lineage MUST possess one stable lineage identity distinct from the identities of its member generations.
A Protocol Generation MUST be included in a lineage only through an explicit lineage-membership rule supported by the applicable succession structure.
A Protocol Lineage MUST preserve the separate identities and lifecycle records of all member generations.
A Protocol Lineage MUST NOT create, inherit, transfer, or replace the protocol authority of any member generation.

A Protocol Lineage model MUST permit independent Protocol Generations to remain in separate Protocol Lineages and MUST require an explicit succession relationship before placing generations in one lineage.
Lineage membership MUST NOT by itself be interpreted as compatibility, migration eligibility, deprecation, replacement, or semantic equivalence.
Every published Protocol Generation MUST possess a stable version designation sufficient to distinguish it from every other published generation.
A version designation MUST NOT by itself be interpreted as proof of compatibility, incompatibility, succession, migration eligibility, or semantic equivalence.
A change to protocol-defined semantics, obligations, validity, invariants, or permitted behavior MUST be represented by a distinct Protocol Generation.
Semantic change MUST NOT be introduced through silent mutation, editorial replacement, implementation variation, or reinterpretation of an existing Published Protocol.

scope: Every classification of a protocol change
text: A protocol change MUST be classified according to its semantic effect rather than only its label, release number, implementation impact, or publication format.
A claim of compatible evolution MUST identify the generations, requirements, subjects, and compatibility scope to which the claim applies.

scope: Every implementation variation within one published generation
text: An implementation variation MAY occur without a new Protocol Generation only when every applicable protocol semantic and normative requirement remains preserved.
A compatible successor generation MUST remain distinctly identified and MUST preserve every predecessor obligation included within the declared compatibility scope.
Breaking evolution MUST be represented by a distinct successor generation and MUST explicitly identify the affected compatibility boundary.
Compatibility MUST NOT be used to merge generation identities, mutate historical published truth, or conceal semantic change.
Deprecation MUST identify the deprecated generation, the effective lifecycle condition, and any published continuation or migration guidance.
Deprecation MUST NOT revoke, erase, mutate, or retroactively invalidate the identity, published content, or historical truth of the deprecated generation.
A published migration MUST identify its source target, destination target, applicability conditions, required steps, preserved properties, and explicit failure conditions.
A mandatory migration obligation MUST be expressed as an identified normative requirement with explicit applicability and requirement strength.
Migration MUST NOT mutate the identity of a Protocol Generation, Published Protocol, implementation target, conformance determination, or certification.
A deprecation or migration statement MUST NOT silently redefine compatibility, succession, lineage membership, or protocol semantics.

scope: Every environment supporting multiple published Protocol Generations
text: Coexisting Protocol Generations MUST remain separately identifiable and MUST retain separate applicability, compatibility, lifecycle, and authority records.
Coexistence MUST NOT be interpreted as semantic equivalence, automatic compatibility, shared identity, succession, or migration eligibility.
Retirement MUST identify the retired generation, retirement scope, effective condition, and consequences for future implementation, assessment, and support.
Retirement MUST NOT delete, mutate, conceal, or retroactively invalidate the retired generation or its historical protocol truth.
Deprecation, migration, coexistence, and retirement MUST be interpreted as distinct bounded lifecycle concepts.

scope: Every use of a canonical Protocol Specification term
text: A canonical term MUST be interpreted according to its definition and bounded role in this specification.

scope: Every downstream section, profile, implementation, application adapter, assessment, and supporting artifact
text: Every downstream use of a canonical term MUST preserve the same subject, relationship, scope, and identity distinction established by this specification.

scope: Every term that may denote either a protocol type or an occurrence
text: A term that may denote either a type or an occurrence MUST explicitly preserve the applicable type-or-occurrence distinction.

scope: Every specification definition involving a semantic subject, identifier, or representation
text: The terminology used for a semantic subject, its identifier, and its representation MUST preserve those as distinct concepts.

scope: Every alias, abbreviation, implementation name, application label, and editorial synonym
text: An alias, abbreviation, implementation name, application label, or editorial synonym MUST NOT silently redefine, merge, widen, or narrow a canonical protocol term.

scope: Every terminology decision and editorial reorganization
text: Terminology or editorial structure MUST NOT introduce a new first-class protocol subject, lifecycle, authority, or semantic boundary.

scope: Every permitted local alias for a canonical protocol term
text: A permitted local alias MUST map explicitly and unambiguously to exactly one canonical term while preserving its protocol meaning.
Every established identified protocol subject MUST retain its own bounded identity according to its defined architectural role.

scope: Every Protocol Action, Protocol Action Evaluation, Protocol Action Determination, and Protocol State Transition
text: Protocol Action, Evaluation, Determination, and Protocol State Transition identities MUST remain mutually distinct.

scope: Every Protocol Action Evaluation and its Protocol Action Determination
text: Evaluation and Determination MUST retain distinct process and result identities while remaining two bounded aspects of one architectural model.

scope: Every Protocol Operation and associated Protocol Action
text: A Protocol Operation capability and each Protocol Action occurrence classified by it MUST remain distinct.

scope: Every Protocol Transition and governed Protocol State Transition
text: A Protocol Transition mapping and each Protocol State Transition occurrence governed by it MUST remain distinct.

scope: Every relationship between identified protocol subjects
text: Every subject relationship MUST preserve its declared direction, bounded meaning, and participating subject identities.

scope: Every protocol subject referenced through an implementation, application, runtime mechanism, or application interpretation
text: A protocol subject MUST remain distinct from the implementation, application, runtime mechanism, and application-defined meaning through which it is represented or used.

scope: Every downstream representation or reference to an established protocol subject
text: Every downstream representation or reference MUST preserve the identity of the same established protocol subject rather than substitute a newly inferred subject.

scope: Every relationship, composition, representation, and implementation convenience involving distinct subjects
text: A relationship, composition, representation, or implementation convenience MUST NOT silently merge distinct protocol subjects or their identities.

scope: Every proposed extension to the established protocol-subject inventory
text: A proposed extension MUST NOT introduce a new first-class subject unless independent identity, meaning, semantic ownership, and irreducible lifecycle necessity are all established.
Every protocol identifier MUST possess one declared bounded role identifying exactly the subject or occurrence specified by that role.

scope: Every identified protocol subject and its identifier
text: A protocol subject and the identifier used to reference it MUST remain distinct.

scope: Every protocol subject and its syntactic, serialized, stored, transmitted, or displayed representation
text: A semantic protocol subject and each representation of it MUST remain distinct.

scope: Every relationship between separately identified protocol subjects
text: The identifier of one related protocol subject MUST NOT be substituted for the identifier of another subject.

scope: Every identifier of a Protocol Action occurrence
text: A Protocol Action identifier MUST NOT identify, encode, imply, or reconstruct the Private Actor who performed the action.

scope: Every public Evaluation, Determination, and Protocol State Transition identifier
text: An Evaluation, Determination, or Protocol State Transition identifier MUST NOT identify, encode, imply, or reconstruct a Private Actor.

scope: Every implementation, transaction, retry, transport-attempt, storage, or diagnostic identifier
text: An operational identifier MUST NOT silently become or redefine a protocol-subject or occurrence identifier.

scope: Every protocol identifier outside its declared subject and context
text: A protocol identifier MUST NOT be reused outside its declared role as a universal participant identifier, cross-subject join key, or cross-action identity mechanism.

scope: Every permitted change of protocol-subject representation
text: A representation change MUST preserve the identity, semantics, relationships, and bounded identifier role of the represented protocol subject.
Every registry, mapping, profile, authorization, U, comparison attempt, definition and recovery table MUST have one identity satisfying its declared grammar.
Every registry, mapping, profile, authorization, U, comparison attempt, definition and recovery table MUST remain distinct from every other identity class.
Every comparison attempt identity MUST be occurrence-local, contiguous within U and immutable with its result.

scope: Every Privacy Engine realization of a public protocol action
text: Every realization MUST preserve the architectural principle `Private actors, public actions`.
A publicly visible Protocol Action MUST remain verifiable to its declared protocol extent without disclosure of the Private Actor.

scope: Every relationship between a Private Actor and a public Protocol Action
text: The performer relationship MUST preserve the Private Actor and Protocol Action as distinct subjects.
A public protocol-subject identifier MUST identify only its declared protocol subject and role.
A public protocol consequence MUST remain attributable to the applicable public protocol occurrence without becoming attributable to a disclosed Private Actor.

scope: Every Protocol Action validity, authorization, uniqueness, and public-consequence rule
text: A rule governing a public Protocol Action MUST NOT require disclosure of civil, wallet, enrollment, admission, application, implementation, deployment, or transport identity as Private Actor identity.

scope: Every public Privacy Engine protocol surface
text: A public protocol surface MUST NOT require or create a reusable public participant identity.

scope: Every Privacy Engine protocol action governed by anonymous-participation semantics
text: The protocol action MUST permit verification of its applicable validity properties without disclosure of the Private Actor.

scope: Every public value and public protocol subject exposed by an anonymous action
text: Private Actor identity MUST remain non-inferable from each exposed value or subject within the protocol-defined privacy boundary.

scope: Every pair or collection of anonymous Protocol Actions in distinct action contexts
text: Cross-action unlinkability MUST be preserved unless the published protocol generation expressly defines a narrower public relationship that remains non-identifying.

scope: Every wallet identifier, wallet signature, wallet-derived value, and wallet relationship
text: Wallet identity MUST NOT be substituted for, used to infer, or represented as anonymous membership identity or Private Actor identity.

scope: Every application identifier, account, profile, metadata value, and application-defined relationship
text: Application identity or application metadata MUST NOT be substituted for, used to infer, or represented as protocol identity or Private Actor identity.

scope: Every implementation identifier and implementation-specific internal value
text: Implementation identity or internal implementation context MUST NOT be substituted for, used to infer, or represented as protocol identity or Private Actor identity.

scope: Every deployment identifier, topology coordinate, service identity, and infrastructure relationship
text: Deployment identity or infrastructure topology MUST NOT be substituted for, used to infer, or represented as protocol identity or Private Actor identity.

scope: Every transport identifier, connection attribute, delivery path, retry path, and request context
text: Transport identity or delivery context MUST NOT be substituted for, used to infer, or represented as protocol identity or Private Actor identity.

scope: Every enrollment right, admission object, funding relationship, sponsor relationship, and associated provenance
text: Enrollment, admission, funding, or sponsor provenance MUST NOT be carried into public-action identity or used as an action-layer correlation value.
An action-local public value MUST remain bounded to its declared action role, action context, and permitted protocol interpretation.
Failure handling MUST preserve Private Actor non-disclosure and the non-identity-bearing role of public values.

scope: Every implementation, profile, application, conformance claim, diagnostic, and specification interpretation
text: A Privacy Engine artifact MUST NOT claim anonymity, unlinkability, metadata protection, or transport protection beyond the bounded guarantees of the identified published protocol generation.
Every mapping profile MUST project only the minimum protocol-owned components required by T.
A projection, authorization or comparison MUST NOT contain Private Actor identity, admission or enrollment provenance, reusable participant identity or an actor-reconstruction bridge.
A blinded component opening MUST remain confidential.
A blinded component opening MUST be disclosed only inside an authorized comparison or independent privacy-validation boundary.
Component identifiers, commitments and result identifiers MUST be assessed in composition for uniqueness, correlation and cross-action linkage before profile admission.
Failure, recovery, retry and observability surfaces MUST preserve Private actors, public actions.
Failure, recovery, retry and observability surfaces MUST NOT expand disclosure.

scope: Every composition of publicly exposed Privacy Engine values, subjects, consequences, and records
text: The composition MUST remain non-identifying for the Private Actor within the protocol-defined privacy boundary.

scope: Every implementation-controlled identifier, timing label, diagnostic, serialization field, log field, storage key, route, and public response
text: An implementation-controlled surface MUST NOT create an actor-reconstruction, provenance, or unauthorized cross-action correlation bridge.

scope: Every privacy-sensitive field name, variable name, route name, log label, diagnostic, comment, example, test, serialization field, and specification term
text: Privacy-sensitive naming and documentation MUST use neutral terminology that preserves non-attribution and the bounded role of each value.
Public observability MUST expose only the minimum role-bounded information required by the applicable protocol semantics.
A diagnostic MUST describe only the applicable protocol subject, status, or bounded failure classification without identifying or reconstructing the Private Actor.

scope: Every request history, telemetry record, path-acquisition record, submission record, and operational history
text: Operational history or telemetry MUST NOT create a persistent relationship linking private participation across protocol layers or action contexts.

scope: Every public protocol response, log, status surface, and diagnostic
text: A public surface MUST NOT expose unnecessary provenance, topology, route, provider, retry, fallback, or execution-path information capable of increasing actor correlation.

scope: Every information crossing between Privacy Engine layers
text: A layer boundary MUST pass only the minimum preserved output required by the receiving layer without carrying unrelated provenance or identity context from the preceding layer.

scope: Every implementation composition exposing multiple individually non-identifying surfaces
text: The combined surface MUST be assessed and preserved as non-identifying rather than relying only on the independent safety of each component.

scope: Every informative example, supporting cross-reference, test artifact, assessment record, and documentation surface
text: Supporting or informative material MUST NOT introduce a correlation or identity interpretation prohibited from normative runtime surfaces.
Public comparison output MUST be limited to U's action-bounded identity and exactly one bounded result or failure classification.
A comparison result MUST NOT become an independent first-class protocol subject or reusable public participant identifier.
Diagnostics, logs, events, databases and application observations MUST remain non-authoritative for comparison, recovery and commitment.
An observability surface MUST NOT disclose a blind, opening, confidential canonical component or actor-bearing correlation value.
Absence or inconsistency of non-authoritative observability MUST NOT alter an authoritative comparison result or occurrence state.

scope: Every anonymous membership identity in the current published protocol generation
text: Anonymous membership identity MUST derive solely from private `memberSecret` possession through `leaf = Poseidon1(memberSecret)`.

scope: Every claim of anonymous membership continuity
text: Anonymous membership continuity MUST mean possession of the same original `memberSecret`.

scope: Every replacement of an active `memberSecret` with a different secret
text: A different `memberSecret` MUST establish a different anonymous membership identity.

scope: Every wallet, backend, application, deployment, transport, and heuristic recovery mechanism
text: A mechanism other than possession of the same original `memberSecret` MUST NOT establish, reconstruct, or simulate anonymous membership continuity.
A membership leaf MUST remain bounded to membership inclusion, path acquisition, and private proof-witness use according to the applicable protocol semantics.
Enrollment or activation MUST attach membership only to the privately controlled membership material presented for that enrollment without importing funding provenance into membership identity.

scope: Every enrollment right, admission object, funding wallet, sponsor relationship, and accounting state
text: An enrollment or admission artifact MUST NOT be represented as anonymous membership identity or Private Actor identity.

scope: Every public enrollment, membership-status, readiness, and application surface
text: A public surface MUST NOT expose a reusable mapping from enrollment or admission provenance to anonymous membership or public action occurrence.

scope: Every anonymous action type requiring one action per member per action context
text: Uniqueness MUST be enforced within the declared `(actionId, member)` scope.

scope: Every nullifier in the current published protocol generation
text: A nullifier MUST be derived as `Poseidon3(memberSecret, actionId, SIGN_DOMAIN)`.

scope: Every action-layer duplicate-prevention decision in the current published protocol generation
text: Nullifier status MUST remain the sole action-layer duplicate-prevention primitive.

scope: Every public nullifier and nullifier-status record
text: A nullifier or its status MUST NOT be represented as Private Actor identity or reusable participant identity.

scope: Every wallet identifier, membership leaf, enrollment identifier, admission object, and application account
text: A wallet, leaf, enrollment, admission, or application identifier MUST NOT replace the nullifier as the action-layer uniqueness key.

scope: Every duplicate-status response, log, diagnostic, event, and read model
text: Duplicate-status observability MUST NOT disclose or enable inference of the Private Actor beyond the bounded action-local uniqueness fact.
Scoped nullifier uniqueness MUST NOT be represented as one-person, one-human, one-wallet, or globally reusable participant uniqueness.
An Interface Contract MUST possess one stable identity, one bounded semantic role, and one version sufficient to distinguish its published meaning.
An Interface Contract MUST derive from exactly one identified published Privacy Engine protocol generation.
An Interface Contract MUST define its bounded input semantics, output semantics, Protocol Operations, externally relied-upon behavior, and applicable observable failure semantics.

scope: Every Interface Contract and every concrete realization of it
text: Interface meaning and concrete representation MUST remain distinct semantic and syntactic roles.
A Concrete Interface Specification MUST possess one stable specification identity, one specification version, and one bounded integration surface.
A Concrete Interface Specification MUST identify and realize exactly one governing Interface Contract.

A Concrete Interface Specification MUST completely define the operation names, invocation forms, field ordering, type constraints, encoding rules, result representations, and externally observable error representations required by its bounded surface.

scope: Every Concrete Interface Specification and its governing Interface Contract
text: The concrete representation MUST preserve semantic equivalence with the governing Interface Contract.

scope: Every Interface Contract permitting multiple concrete realizations
text: Multiple Concrete Interface Specifications MAY realize the same Interface Contract when each realization independently preserves the complete bounded interface meaning.
A representation-only change MUST preserve the identity, semantics, ordering requirements, compatibility boundary, and observable guarantees of the governing Interface Contract.

scope: Every change to published Interface Contract meaning
text: A change to published interface semantics, obligations, validity, or observable guarantees MUST be represented through the applicable distinct-generation and versioning rules.

scope: Every Interface Contract and Concrete Interface Specification
text: Implementation algorithms, storage layouts, deployment topology, transport machinery, operational policy, and application-defined meaning MUST NOT become interface semantics unless the published protocol generation expressly defines them as such.

scope: Every Interface Contract and Concrete Interface Specification
text: An Interface Contract or Concrete Interface Specification MUST NOT independently acquire, transfer, replace, or modify protocol authority.

scope: Every public Interface Contract and Concrete Interface Specification
text: Every public interface realization MUST preserve the applicable SF-03 and SF-04 identity, privacy, unlinkability, minimum-disclosure, and neutral-naming requirements.

An interface, adapter or implementation MUST NOT define a predicate, infer a missing coordinate, select recovery or substitute an implementation value for authoritative protocol state.
A public interface MUST NOT carry a confidential opening unless that interface is the authenticated confidential comparison boundary defined by the profile.
A Protocol Surface MUST possess one stable identity and one bounded externally relied-upon capability scope within one published protocol generation.
A Protocol Surface MUST expose only the protocol capabilities, semantic guarantees, compatibility boundaries, and observable behavior defined for that surface.

scope: Every implementation realizing a Protocol Surface
text: Internal implementation machinery MUST remain replaceable when the complete published semantics and guarantees of the Protocol Surface remain preserved.

scope: Every implementation detail behind a Protocol Surface
text: Code structure, storage layout, deployment topology, relay selection, transport, persistence, monitoring, optimization, or helper naming MUST NOT become protocol-surface semantics merely because a current implementation uses it.
A Protocol Operation MUST possess one stable capability identity defined by one published Interface Contract within one identified protocol generation.
A Protocol Operation MUST define one bounded protocol-owned capability, including its applicable input meaning, output meaning, and externally relied-upon behavior.

scope: Every Protocol Operation and associated Protocol Action
text: The exposed Protocol Operation and associated Protocol Action representation MUST preserve the RF-07 distinction between the Protocol Operation capability type and each Protocol Action occurrence classified by that capability.
The governing Interface Contract MUST declare the operation's applicability conditions and the semantic roles of every required input and Published Result.

scope: Every implementation realizing a Protocol Operation
text: An implementation MUST preserve the operation's published capability across execution and implementation variation.

scope: Every execution or implementation variation realizing a Protocol Operation
text: Execution or implementation variation MUST NOT redefine the Protocol Operation's published capability.
A Published Result MUST possess one bounded result identity and MUST identify the governing Interface Contract and Protocol Operation from which its meaning derives.
A Published Result MUST express only the interface-level success semantics, failure semantics, guarantees, and observable meaning defined by its governing Interface Contract.

scope: Every Published Result and concrete representation of it
text: Published Result meaning and its serialized, transported, stored, displayed, or application-facing representation MUST remain distinct.

scope: Every concrete realization or translation of a Published Result
text: Every concrete realization or permitted downstream translation MUST preserve the complete bounded meaning of the same Published Result.
A Published Result MUST NOT be represented as a Protocol Action Evaluation, Protocol Action Determination, acceptance object, rejection object, or separate Evaluation Outcome object.
A Published Result MUST NOT be represented as a committed Protocol State Transition or as an independently authoritative public protocol-state consequence.

scope: Every application interpretation or representation of a Protocol Surface, Protocol Operation, or Published Result
text: Application-defined meaning, terminology, formatting, workflow, or response structure MUST NOT redefine protocol capability, validity, or Published Result meaning.

scope: Every public Protocol Surface, Protocol Operation representation, and Published Result
text: The complete exposed composition MUST preserve the applicable SF-03 and SF-04 identity, privacy, unlinkability, minimum-disclosure, and forbidden-correlation requirements.

scope: Every Determination and every later representation or realization of it
text: Protocol-semantic Determination production MUST remain distinct from representation, serialization, persistence, publication, transport, operational delivery, display, indexing, events, logs, responses and application interpretation.

text: Every completed comparison attempt MUST produce exactly one of equivalent, material-conflict or indeterminate.
A represented comparison result MUST preserve its exact authoritative classification and U binding without expanding its evidentiary claim.
A commitment digest MUST establish only computational binding of its encoded preimage under the identified algorithm.
A commitment digest MUST NOT prove any unencoded semantic or identity claim.

scope: Every proof required by a Privacy Engine Protocol Action
text: A proof MUST possess one bounded evidence identity distinct from its encoding, public inputs, private witness, supported Protocol Action, and Private Actor.

scope: Every proof type in a published protocol generation
text: The published protocol generation MUST declare the proof relation, proof-system requirements, public-input schema, private-witness boundary, and verification semantics applicable to the proof type.

The proof relation MUST establish knowledge of the applicable membership secret and membership witness, inclusion under the declared membership root, and correct nullifier derivation for the declared action context without disclosing the Private Actor.

scope: Every proof relation and proof-construction boundary
text: Public inputs and private witness material MUST remain explicitly separated according to the applicable published proof relation.
The declared public inputs MUST occur in the exact ordered sequence `nullifier`, `petitionId` or `actionId`, `membershipRoot`.

`nullifier` MUST remain bounded to action-context uniqueness, `petitionId` or `actionId` MUST remain bounded to action context, and `membershipRoot` MUST remain bounded to the applicable membership-state commitment.

scope: Every proof and declared public-input set presented together
text: The proof representation, public-input values, ordering, action context, and proof relation MUST form one coherent verification input.
Proof construction MUST keep `memberSecret`, Merkle path, membership leaf, and other private witness material outside public inputs and public protocol surfaces.

scope: Every proof realization for the current published generation
text: The proof realization MUST use the published generation's declared Circom and Groth16-over-BN254 proof semantics and compatible verifier artifacts.
Proof artifacts, verification keys, verifier artifacts, public-input ordering, and associated provenance MUST satisfy the published artifact-integrity and reproducibility requirements.

scope: Every permitted proof or public-input representation
text: A representation MUST preserve the complete proof relation, proof-system semantics, verifier compatibility, input meaning, and input ordering of the identified published generation.

scope: Every change to a proof system, proof relation, public-input schema, public-input ordering, verifier encoding, or artifact-integrity rule
text: The change MUST follow the applicable distinct-generation, versioning, publication, and artifact-regeneration requirements.
A proof or its representation MUST NOT be treated as the Protocol Action occurrence, Private Actor identity, wallet identity, membership identity, application truth, or reusable participant identity.

scope: Every declared public input and public-input composition
text: A public input or public-input composition MUST NOT exceed its declared role or become a reusable participant identifier, cross-action join key, actor-reconstruction value, or application-only correlation field.
Proof verification MUST occur as one bounded verification occurrence whose proof, public inputs, proof relation, verifier artifacts, and result are distinguishable.
Verification MUST evaluate exactly the presented proof and declared public-input set against the applicable published proof relation and verifier artifacts.
Verification MUST be deterministic for the same proof, public inputs, proof relation, verifier artifacts, and protocol-relevant verification context.
A completed verification MUST produce exactly one bounded proof-valid or proof-invalid classification.
A proof-valid classification MUST establish only that the proof and declared public inputs satisfy the applicable published proof relation.

scope: Every proof-invalid classification required for a Protocol Action
text: A required proof-invalid classification MUST prevent that proof from satisfying the corresponding applicable proof-verification requirement.

scope: Every inability to complete required proof verification
text: Verification failure MUST remain distinguishable from a completed proof-valid classification, completed proof-invalid classification, Protocol Action rejection, and later failure classifications.

scope: Every proof-valid verification result used in Protocol Action Evaluation
text: The result MUST contribute only the bounded evidence established by the applicable proof relation.
Successful proof verification MUST NOT independently establish complete Protocol Action validity, acceptance, rejection, transition authorization, transition execution, or commitment.

Proof verification MUST NOT establish Private Actor identity, wallet identity, enrollment provenance, admission provenance, application truth, legal truth, factual truth, or reusable participant identity.

Verifier code structure, deployment address, transaction identity, runtime mechanism, storage, transport, or diagnostic behavior MUST NOT redefine the applicable proof relation or verification semantics.
A proof-verification component or result MUST NOT independently acquire or modify protocol authority.

scope: Every proof-verification result used during Protocol Action Evaluation
text: The result MUST remain bounded evidence concerning exactly the proof relation and public-input relationship evaluated by that verification occurrence.

scope: Every proof-verification result contributing to complete Evaluation
text: The result MUST contribute to the later Protocol Action Evaluation without replacing the Action, applicable rule set, Evaluation, or Determination.

scope: Every Protocol Action validity determination basis
text: Complete Protocol Action validity MUST mean satisfaction of every applicable protocol rule within one bounded evaluation context.
Successful proof verification MUST NOT be represented as complete Protocol Action validity unless proof verification constitutes the complete applicable protocol-rule set for that action and context.

scope: Every Protocol Action whose applicable rule set includes non-proof validity conditions
text: Every applicable non-proof validity condition MUST remain represented and evaluated as part of the complete applicable protocol-rule set.
A non-proof validity condition MUST derive from the identified published protocol generation and MUST possess a bounded applicability rule for the affected action and context.

scope: Every current-generation Protocol Action Evaluation basis
text: The applicable validity basis MUST account for required action shape, public-input coherence, accepted-root status, nullifier uniqueness, replay prevention, domain separation, protocol-state requirements, and every other applicable generation-derived condition.
A required proof-invalid result MUST prevent the Protocol Action from satisfying the corresponding applicable proof requirement.
Protocol validity MUST remain action-specific, applicable-rule-relative, and bounded to the identified evaluation context.
Proof validity or protocol validity MUST NOT independently become Protocol Action acceptance, rejection, transition authorization, transition execution, or commitment.

scope: Every protocol-valid Protocol Action and interpretation of it
text: Protocol validity MUST NOT be represented as application truth, external factual truth, legal truth, social truth, institutional recognition, or a Protocol Claim.

scope: Every evidence, validity, failure, and diagnostic surface
text: The surface MUST preserve SF-03 and SF-04 identity separation, Private Actor non-disclosure, role-bounded public values, neutral naming, and compositional unlinkability.

A Protocol Action MUST be one bounded occurrence of protocol-defined behavior presented through an implementation for Evaluation under the applicable rules of one identified published protocol generation.
Each Protocol Action MUST possess one stable occurrence identity distinct from every other Protocol Action occurrence.
The Action MUST be bounded to one occurrence, one action type, one declared public-input set, one applicable protocol-rule set, and one bounded evaluation context.
The occurrence MUST identify its protocol-defined action type and governing published protocol generation.

scope: Every Protocol Operation, action type, and Protocol Action occurrence
text: Published capability, action-type classification, and individual action occurrence MUST remain distinct.

scope: Every effort to construct, present, submit, or obtain evaluation of a candidate Protocol Action
text: An action attempt MUST remain distinct from a Protocol Action occurrence admitted to the authoritative evaluation boundary.

scope: Every candidate admitted to authoritative Protocol Action Evaluation
text: Admission to the applicable authoritative evaluation boundary MUST instantiate one bounded Protocol Action occurrence without identifying its Private Actor.

scope: Every transport retry, relay attempt, submission retry, implementation retry, and internal processing attempt
text: An operational retry or attempt MUST NOT silently widen, replace, merge, or create the identity of the logical Protocol Action occurrence.

scope: Every protocol rule governing repeated authoritative presentations
text: The rule MUST determine whether the presentations concern one action occurrence or distinct action occurrences without inferring or merging Private Actor identity.
The Action MUST carry exactly the declared public-input set required for its action type while remaining distinct from those public inputs.
The Action and its supporting proof MUST remain distinct, and the proof MUST contribute only its bounded evidence role.

scope: Every Protocol Action performed through an implementation
text: The Action occurrence MUST remain distinct from the implementation, deployment, transaction, transport, storage, and runtime machinery through which it is presented.

scope: Every relationship between a Private Actor and Protocol Action
text: Protocol Action representation, processing, and Evaluation presentation MUST preserve the RF-09 Private Actor and public Protocol Action separation invariant throughout the Action lifecycle.

scope: Every Protocol Action identifier and representation
text: An action identifier or representation MUST NOT identify, encode, imply, reconstruct, or become a reusable identifier for the Private Actor.

scope: Every application interpretation of a Protocol Action
text: Application-defined meaning, terminology, workflow, metadata, or truth MUST NOT become Protocol Action identity or protocol validity.

scope: Every relationship from a Protocol Action to a possible Published Result, Determination, or Protocol State Transition
text: The Protocol Action MUST remain distinct from every interface result, downstream Determination, and possible state-transition consequence.

scope: Every Protocol Action interpretation and extension
text: A Protocol Action MUST NOT be represented as a Protocol Claim or used to introduce another first-class subject without satisfying the established closed-ontology test.
The Action MUST be governed by exactly one complete and bounded applicable protocol-rule set for its identified action type and evaluation context.

scope: Every rule included in an applicable Protocol Action rule set
text: Each applicable rule MUST derive from the identified published protocol generation through the established Protocol Specification and implementation-profile direction.

scope: Every determination of Protocol Action rule applicability
text: Applicability MUST be determined only from protocol-defined action type, applicable implementation profile, protocol-relevant state, and bounded evaluation-context conditions.

scope: Every Protocol Action admitted for authoritative Evaluation
text: The complete applicable protocol-rule set MUST be established before authoritative Evaluation begins.

scope: Every implementation, application, transport, deployment, and operational policy
text: Implementation convenience, application policy, transport behavior, deployment state, or operational discretion MUST NOT silently create, remove, weaken, strengthen, or reinterpret a protocol-validity rule.

scope: Every Protocol Action validity classification basis
text: The validity-classification basis MUST apply the complete RF-18 definition of Protocol Action validity through the complete applicable protocol-rule set within the identified bounded evaluation context without replacing or redefining that definition.

scope: Every applicable Protocol Action rule set
text: The rule set MUST include every applicable proof requirement, public-input requirement, non-proof validity condition, uniqueness condition, state-relative condition, and action-type constraint.

Protocol-rule interpretation and application MUST preserve the RF-18 action-specific, applicable-rule-relative, evaluation-context-bounded validity invariant without widening validity beyond the identified context.

scope: Every comparison of Protocol Action validity across materially different evaluation contexts
text: Validity in one evaluation context MUST NOT be inferred as validity in a materially different evaluation context.

scope: Every application interpretation and external claim associated with a Protocol Action
text: Application meaning, factual meaning, legal meaning, social meaning, or institutional meaning MUST NOT replace or redefine the applicable protocol-rule set or protocol validity.

scope: Every action-local uniqueness or authorization rule
text: The rule MUST preserve the declared action scope without creating reusable participant identity, actor disclosure, or unauthorized cross-action linkage.

scope: Every implementation, transaction, transport, retry, storage, and diagnostic identifier
text: An operational identifier MUST NOT determine, replace, merge, or redefine Protocol Action identity, rule applicability, or protocol validity.

scope: Every Protocol Action prepared for complete Evaluation
text: The Action, complete applicable rule set, and bounded evaluation context MUST be available as distinct preserved inputs to SF-08 without pre-emptively defining Evaluation, Determination, acceptance, or rejection.
A Protocol Action Evaluation MUST possess one stable occurrence identity identifying exactly one bounded Evaluation occurrence.
An Evaluation MUST evaluate exactly one identified Protocol Action.
An Evaluation MUST apply exactly one complete applicable protocol-rule set established for the evaluated Action.
An Evaluation MUST occur within exactly one bounded protocol-relevant evaluation context.

scope: Every candidate entering the authoritative Evaluation boundary
text: Authoritative Evaluation MUST begin only after the Action, complete applicable rule set, and bounded evaluation context have been established as distinct inputs.

scope: Every Protocol Action Evaluation after Evaluation begins
text: The Evaluation MUST preserve its identified Action, complete applicable rule set, and bounded evaluation context throughout the Evaluation.

scope: Every Protocol Action Evaluation after Evaluation begins
text: An Evaluation MUST NOT substitute, merge, widen, narrow, repair, or infer a replacement Action, rule set, or evaluation context.
A complete Evaluation MUST evaluate every applicable protocol rule governing the identified Action in the identified context.
An Evaluation component MUST possess an explicit assignment to one applicable requirement or one bounded subset of the complete applicable rule set.
An Evaluation component MUST evaluate only the applicable requirement or bounded subset assigned to that component.

scope: Every Evaluation component whose assigned rules are not the complete applicable rule set
text: A bounded component MUST NOT be represented as complete Protocol Action Evaluation.

scope: Every Evaluation containing multiple required components
text: The Evaluation MUST coherently combine every required component result before determining whether the Evaluation is complete.

scope: Every proof-verification occurrence contributing to Evaluation
text: Proof verification MUST remain bounded evidence concerning the declared proof relation and declared public inputs.

scope: Every relationship between proof verification and Protocol Action Evaluation
text: Proof verification MUST remain distinct from the complete Evaluation to which it contributes.
A proof-verification result MUST NOT directly produce a Protocol Action Determination, acceptance classification, or rejection classification.

scope: Every Evaluation whose applicable rule set contains non-proof validity conditions
text: The Evaluation MUST evaluate every applicable non-proof validity condition independently of proof-verification success.

scope: Every Protocol Action Evaluation completeness classification
text: An Evaluation MUST be classified as complete exactly when it has evaluated every applicable rule for the identified Action within the identified context.

scope: Every partial or incomplete Protocol Action Evaluation
text: A partial or incomplete Evaluation MUST NOT produce a Determination, acceptance classification, or rejection classification.

scope: Every Evaluation failure and every pre-evaluation failure
text: Evaluation failure or pre-evaluation failure MUST NOT be represented as a completed Evaluation or as producing a Protocol Action Determination.

scope: Every Evaluation component, identifier, evidence record, representation, diagnostic, log, field, route, test, example, and observability surface
text: An Evaluation surface MUST NOT identify the Private Actor, extend evidence into actor identification, introduce reusable participant identity, create cross-action linkage, or create an actor-reconstruction bridge.
Every completed Protocol Action Evaluation MUST produce exactly one Protocol Action Determination as part of the same protocol-semantic completion transition.

scope: Every implementation representation of Evaluation completion and Determination production
text: An implementation MUST NOT represent Evaluation completion and required Determination production as two protocol-semantic transitions separated by a valid completed-Evaluation state.

scope: Every Protocol Action Evaluation completion classification
text: A Protocol Action Evaluation MUST be in a valid completed state exactly when every applicable completion requirement is satisfied and exactly one corresponding Protocol Action Determination has been produced.

scope: Every active incomplete Protocol Action Evaluation
text: An active Protocol Action Evaluation MAY contain bounded internal steps, completed components and intermediate component state while remaining incomplete.

scope: Every internal Evaluation step, component result, intermediate state and readiness condition
text: An internal step, component result, combined intermediate state or completion-readiness condition MUST NOT be represented as completed Evaluation or as a Protocol Action Determination.

scope: Every begun Evaluation unable to establish one valid Determination at its completion boundary
text: If an Evaluation that has begun cannot establish exactly one valid Determination at the same protocol-semantic boundary as Evaluation completion, the Evaluation MUST terminate as Evaluation failure, MUST remain incomplete, and MUST produce no Determination, acceptance or rejection.
A new Evaluation MUST create a new E identity.
A new Evaluation MUST preserve every earlier E and D without mutation.
A new Evaluation MUST produce a new D only if it completes successfully at the Evaluation-completion boundary.
Failure before successful completion of a new Evaluation MUST produce no new D, acceptance, authorization or U.
A Protocol Action Determination MUST possess one stable result identity identifying exactly one bounded Determination.

scope: Every relationship between a Protocol Action Evaluation and its Determination
text: The Evaluation process and resulting Determination MUST remain separately identified and semantically distinct.
A completed Evaluation MUST produce exactly one Protocol Action Determination.
A Determination MUST derive from exactly one completed Protocol Action Evaluation.
A Determination MUST identify exactly one producing completed Evaluation, one evaluated Action, one complete applicable rule set, and one bounded evaluation context.
A valid Determination MUST contain and reference its RF-24 classification without defining an alternative classification model.

scope: Every incomplete or failed Protocol Action Evaluation
text: An incomplete or failed Evaluation MUST NOT be treated as possessing or producing a Protocol Action Determination.

scope: Every Protocol Action Determination and proof-verification result
text: A Determination MUST remain distinct from every proof-verification occurrence and proof-verification result contributing to its Evaluation.

scope: Every Protocol Action Determination and Published Result
text: A Determination MUST remain distinct from every interface-level Published Result and its concrete representation.

scope: Every Protocol Action Determination and possible Protocol State Transition
text: A Determination MUST remain distinct from transition identity, transition execution, commitment, and every committed public protocol-state consequence.

scope: Every Determination identifier, representation, diagnostic, log, field, route, test, example, and observability surface
text: A Determination surface MUST NOT identify the Private Actor, become reusable participant identity, create cross-action linkage, or create an actor-reconstruction bridge.

scope: Every pair of correct Evaluations of the same Action under the same applicable rules and equivalent contexts
text: The Evaluations MUST produce equivalent acceptance or rejection Determinations.
The Determination MUST remain bounded to its identified evaluation context without converting material context differences into implementation discretion.
A Determination MUST NOT be represented as an Evaluation Outcome object or as an independently authoritative source of protocol semantics.

scope: Every protocol state representing Evaluation completion
text: A protocol state MUST NOT contain a completed Protocol Action Evaluation without exactly one corresponding Protocol Action Determination.

scope: Every Evaluation and Determination identity boundary
text: Atomic establishment of Evaluation completion and Determination production MUST preserve the distinct identities and meanings of the Evaluation process and Determination result.
A valid Determination MUST record exactly one mutually exclusive acceptance or rejection classification.
Acceptance MUST mean that completed Evaluation established satisfaction of every applicable protocol rule within the identified evaluation context.
Rejection MUST mean that completed Evaluation established non-satisfaction of at least one applicable protocol rule within the identified evaluation context.
The Determination MUST accept the Action exactly when the Action is protocol-valid within the identified evaluation context.
The Determination MUST reject the Action exactly when the Action is not protocol-valid within the identified evaluation context.

scope: Every incomplete Evaluation, Evaluation failure, and pre-evaluation failure
text: An incomplete Evaluation, Evaluation failure, or pre-evaluation failure MUST NOT be classified as acceptance or rejection.

scope: Every infrastructure, transport, deployment, storage, implementation, and observability failure
text: An operational or implementation failure MUST NOT be represented as protocol rejection.

scope: Every proof-invalid result considered outside complete Protocol Action Evaluation
text: A proof-invalid result alone MUST NOT be represented as a complete rejecting Determination.

scope: Every erroneous acceptance or rejection classification
text: An incorrect classification MUST NOT redefine the applicable rules, protocol validity, or protocol semantics.
Acceptance or rejection MUST NOT be represented as a separately identified acceptance object, rejection object, or Evaluation Outcome object.

scope: Every application or external interpretation of acceptance or rejection
text: Acceptance or rejection MUST NOT be treated as establishing application, factual, legal, social, or institutional truth.

scope: Every acceptance or rejection representation, identifier, diagnostic, log, field, route, test, example, and observability surface
text: An acceptance or rejection classification MUST NOT identify the Private Actor, introduce reusable participant identity, create cross-action linkage, or create an actor-reconstruction bridge.
The applicable protocol rules MUST determine whether the accepted Determination requires no authorized Protocol State Transition.

scope: Every accepted Determination for which no transition is required
text: The Determination MUST terminate successfully without an authorized Protocol State Transition.
The path MUST be treated as a complete successful terminal path at the Determination boundary.

An accepted no-transition path MUST NOT be represented as rejection, incomplete Evaluation, Evaluation failure, pre-transition failure, transition failure, incomplete execution, missing commitment, or implementation error.

scope: Every inference from Protocol Action acceptance
text: Acceptance alone MUST NOT be treated as establishing that a Protocol State Transition exists.

scope: Every inference from Protocol Action acceptance
text: Acceptance alone MUST NOT be treated as transition authorization.

scope: Every inference from Protocol Action acceptance
text: Acceptance alone MUST NOT be treated as transition execution or commitment.
A rejecting Determination MUST NOT authorize a transition that requires an accepted Determination.

scope: Every implementation handling an accepted no-transition path
text: An implementation MUST NOT invent a transition, report missing commitment, or reinterpret the protocol-defined absence of a transition as failure.
A Protocol Transition mapping MUST possess one stable mapping identity within the applicable published protocol generation.
The mapping MUST define the permitted semantic relation between its applicable pre-transition-state class and its protocol-defined successor-state class.

scope: Every Protocol Transition mapping and every interpretation of it
text: A Protocol Transition mapping MUST NOT be represented as one Protocol State Transition occurrence, execution, commitment, history entry, or actor occurrence.

scope: Every implementation applying a Protocol Transition mapping
text: The implementation MUST preserve the mapping identity and published transition semantics unchanged.

scope: Every published Protocol Transition mapping with transition-specific preconditions
text: The mapping MUST identify the complete published precondition set governing its eligibility.
Eligibility MUST be established against the applicable protocol state, identified mapping, applicable Action context, and complete published transition-precondition set.

scope: Every transition-eligibility evaluation whose complete applicable precondition set is satisfied
text: The eligibility result MUST preserve the identified mapping and permit only the later processing authorized by the applicable protocol rules.

scope: Every transition-eligibility evaluation whose applicable precondition set is not completely satisfied
text: The ineligible result MUST preserve the applicable pre-transition protocol state as unchanged by that attempted transition.
The implementation MUST NOT infer satisfaction, weaken or strengthen a precondition, substitute another condition, repair the applicable state, or derive an alternate mapping.

scope: Every relationship between transition eligibility and complete Protocol Action Evaluation
text: Transition eligibility MUST remain a bounded transition-specific evaluation distinct from the complete Evaluation defined by RF-22.

A transition-enforcement result MUST NOT itself establish acceptance or rejection, create or alter a Determination, authorize or execute a transition occurrence, commit state change, or establish successor state.

scope: Every implementation-local restriction on operation exposure, request handling, or execution capability
text: An implementation-local restriction MUST NOT be represented as a published transition precondition or as changing protocol eligibility semantics.

scope: Every mapping, precondition, eligibility, enforcement, diagnostic, log, field, route, test, example, serialization, and observability surface
text: A transition-mapping or eligibility surface MUST NOT identify the Private Actor, introduce reusable participant identity, create cross-action linkage, or create an actor-reconstruction bridge.
