text: The successor MUST contain exactly one closed transition-mapping registry with the identity and serialization defined by S69.
Each registry row MUST bind one mapping identity, path and digest to one profile identity, path and digest.
Mapping-to-profile cardinality MUST be exactly 1:1.
Mapping and profile ordinals MUST match.
The registry MUST reject duplicates, missing members, digest mismatch, conflicting bindings and unresolved applicability or recovery definitions.
An empty validated registry MUST authorize zero transitions.
An empty validated registry MUST NOT imply missing or inferred mappings.
A mapping MUST NOT be inferred or discovered from an implementation, interface, runtime, storage, application or observed behaviour.
Registry membership, mappings and profiles MUST be immutable within one generation.
Any registry, mapping or profile change MUST require a distinct future Protocol Generation.
Every mapping MUST reference one separate immutable normative equivalence profile and its SHA-256.
Every profile MUST include all scalar, definition, projection and recovery fields required by S70 without blanks or implementation defaults.
Every profile definition MUST resolve to one authoritative successor source anchor and one total deterministic PE-TSE-EXPR-V2 expression.
Every component MUST define its type, representation, canonicalization, normalization, authority, availability, validity, authentication, privacy and observability rules.
Every profile MUST define mutually exclusive equivalence and material-conflict predicates that cover all complete valid inputs.
Every profile MUST define which differences are immaterial.
Every profile MUST prove that each immaterial difference is outside the mapping's materiality boundary.
Every profile MUST define and validate Dep(D) membership and its complete recovery table.
An incomplete, ambiguous, cyclic, non-total or privacy-invalid profile MUST be inadmissible.
An incomplete, ambiguous, cyclic, non-total or privacy-invalid profile MUST authorize no transition.
A Protocol State Transition MUST possess one stable occurrence identity identifying exactly one bounded protocol-governed state-change occurrence.
The occurrence MUST retain one bounded lifecycle across every applicable authorization, execution, commitment, and failure stage.

scope: Every relationship between a Protocol Action and a Protocol State Transition
text: The Action and transition occurrence MUST retain distinct identities and semantic roles.

scope: Every relationship between a Protocol Action Evaluation and a Protocol State Transition
text: The Evaluation and transition occurrence MUST retain distinct identities and semantic roles.

scope: Every relationship between a Protocol Action Determination and a Protocol State Transition
text: The Determination and transition occurrence MUST retain distinct identities and semantic roles.
The occurrence MUST remain distinct from its governing mapping, pre-transition state, successor state, implementation, history representation, and public consequence.

scope: Every authorization, execution, commitment, and failure stage concerning one Protocol State Transition
text: Every stage MUST preserve the identity of the same authorized `U`.
Authorization, execution, commitment, or failure MUST NOT be represented as a separately identified first-class transition object.

scope: Every terminal Protocol State Transition classification
text: A terminal transition MUST be classified as committed or transition failure, but not both.

scope: Every authorized transition that has not reached a terminal classification
text: Absence of commitment MUST NOT by itself be represented as transition failure.

scope: Every transition identifier, lifecycle record, representation, diagnostic, log, field, route, test, example, serialization, storage key, and observability surface
text: A transition-occurrence surface MUST NOT identify the Private Actor, carry enrollment or admission provenance, introduce reusable participant identity, create cross-action linkage, or create an actor-reconstruction bridge.
Each comparison attempt MUST bind one successor generation, mapping, profile, authorization, D, Q0 and U.
Comparison ordinals MUST begin at 000001 and be contiguous within U.
Each attempt and result MUST remain immutable history of U.
Each attempt and result MUST have no lifecycle independent of U.

scope: Every authorization of a Protocol State Transition arising from a Protocol Action
text: The transition MUST be authorized by one accepted Protocol Action Determination.

scope: Every rejected Determination, incomplete Evaluation, Evaluation failure, and absence of Determination
text: The condition MUST NOT authorize an accepted Protocol State Transition.
Authorization MUST identify the authorizing Determination, authorized `U`, governing `T`, applicable `Q0`, required successor-state relation, and every protocol-defined ordering or dependency.
Authorization MUST select one sufficiently bounded transition occurrence rather than a class of later implementation-selected outcomes.
Acceptance MUST NOT by itself be represented as establishing transition authorization or that a transition occurrence exists.
Authorization MUST NOT be represented as transition execution.
Authorization MUST NOT be represented as transition commitment.
Authorization MUST NOT be represented as an authoritative protocol-state change or authoritative successor state.

scope: Every accepted Determination for which transition cardinality is applicable
text: The complete applicable protocol rules MUST determine whether the Determination authorizes zero, exactly one, or multiple transition occurrences.
The implementation MUST NOT choose transition cardinality for convenience, preferred outcome, infrastructure capability, or implementation policy.

scope: Every accepted Determination requiring zero transitions
text: The zero-transition authorization relation MUST preserve the successful terminal behavior defined by RF-25 without fabricating a transition occurrence.

scope: Every accepted Determination authorizing multiple independently committable effects
text: Each independently committable effect MUST remain one separately identified and separately atomic transition occurrence.

scope: Every accepted Determination authorizing multiple transitions with protocol-defined ordering or dependencies
text: Every authorized ordering and dependency MUST be preserved across the separately identified transitions.

scope: Every group of protocol-required state effects that must succeed or fail together
text: The effects MUST be represented as one composite atomic Protocol State Transition rather than as independently committable transitions.

scope: Every authorization of multiple separately identified Protocol State Transitions
text: Multiple authorized transitions MUST NOT be represented as a separately identified first-class transition-set object.
Every authorization MUST use the canonical header and component-binding serialization defined by S71.
The authorization header MUST bind generation, mapping and digest, profile and digest, authorization, U, D, Q0, successor-state relation, coordinate-set digests and component count.
Ordering and dependency coordinate sets MUST be canonically serialized and digest-bound even when empty.
Each component binding mode MUST be fixed by the published profile.
Each component binding mode MUST NOT be chosen per execution.
Canonical-value mode MUST bind the exact normalized canonical bytes without implying public disclosure.
Blinded mode MUST bind authorization context, component identity, canonical type, canonical bytes and one independent 32-octet blind under PE-TSE-SHA256-COMMITMENT-V1.
Commitment opening MUST authenticate its source, recompute every bound coordinate and require exact digest equality before semantic comparison.
Missing, invalid, unauthenticated or mismatched authorization material MUST yield indeterminate and prohibit execution and commitment.
Execution MUST be the bounded implementation activity that attempts to realize one already-authorized `U`.
Execution MUST begin only where the applicable authorization and transition-eligibility conditions permit execution of the identified `U`.

scope: Every execution of an authorized Protocol State Transition
text: Execution MUST preserve the transition identity, authorizing Determination, governing mapping, authorized pre-transition state, required successor-state relation, atomicity, and complete protocol-defined effects.

scope: Every implementation executing an authorized Protocol State Transition
text: The implementation MUST realize the authorized `U` exactly as defined by the published transition semantics.

scope: Every implementation executing an authorized Protocol State Transition
text: The implementation MUST NOT redefine, reinterpret, widen, narrow, repair, merge, divide, or infer replacement semantics for `U`.
Execution MUST NOT substitute, execute, commit, or report `U'` as `U` where `U' != U`.

scope: Every relationship between transition eligibility and transition execution
text: Eligibility and execution MUST remain distinct stages, with eligibility deciding only whether the already-identified transition may proceed.
Completed execution MUST NOT by itself be represented as commitment or authoritative protocol-state change.

scope: Every successor-state value or representation derived during execution
text: Execution machinery and execution output MUST NOT claim or expose derived successor-state material as committed authoritative protocol state before valid RF-30 commitment.

scope: Every implementation unable to preserve the authorized transition during execution
text: The implementation MUST fail the execution cleanly while preserving the identity and semantics of the authorized `U`.
Execution failure MUST NOT authorize an alternate transition, alternate successor state, partial commitment, or semantic substitution.

scope: Every execution representation, instruction, transaction, internal call, storage operation, retry, diagnostic, log, field, route, test, example, serialization, and observability surface
text: An execution surface MUST NOT create another architectural transition identity, identify the Private Actor, introduce reusable participant identity, create cross-action linkage, or create an actor-reconstruction bridge.
Bounded execution MUST begin only after the immediately preceding comparison returns equivalent.
material-conflict or indeterminate before execution MUST prohibit execution.
Execution failure MUST terminally fail U.
Execution failure MUST prohibit partial commitment, repair, resumption or alternate successor-state substitution.
A later execution attempt MUST use a new U and a valid new authorization selected by the total disposition function.
Commitment MUST be the successful terminal predicate of the same identified `U` that was authorized and executed.
Commitment MUST derive from one valid accepted Determination and valid authorization of `U`.
Commitment MUST follow correct execution that preserves the complete authorized identity and semantics of `U`.

Every committed U authorized against Q0 MUST have produced equivalent under its governing immutable profile at the semantic commitment boundary, after successful bounded execution and without an intervening authoritative protocol-state change.
Commitment MUST establish the complete protocol-defined state-change relation and the required successor state `Q1`.
Commitment MUST establish the absence of omitted required effects and unauthorized additional state effects.
Commitment MUST preserve semantic atomicity across every protocol-required effect owned by `U`.

scope: Every valid authorization and execution context for `U`
text: Commitment MUST be equivalent to complete state change only within that valid bounded context.

scope: Every partial execution of a Protocol State Transition
text: Partial execution MUST NOT be represented as commitment.

scope: Every partial or incomplete state change
text: A partial or incomplete state change MUST NOT be represented as commitment or authoritative successor state.
A transition MUST NOT be partially committed.

scope: Every implementation assertion, report, event, record, diagnostic, or representation concerning commitment
text: The implementation surface MUST NOT by itself establish protocol commitment.
Commitment MUST NOT be represented as a separately identified first-class object or as possessing authority or lifecycle independent of `U`.
Successful execution MUST be followed by authoritative comparison revalidation at the semantic commitment boundary.
Only equivalent at revalidation MUST permit commitment.
material-conflict, indeterminate or revalidation failure after execution MUST terminally fail U and prohibit commitment.
No partial protocol state or alternate successor state from a failed U MUST become authoritative.
Revalidation and commitment MUST form one indivisible protocol-semantic decision without requiring any implementation transaction mechanism.
Protocol state MUST contain only state governed as protocol state by the applicable published protocol generation.

scope: Every application, implementation-local, transport, database, cache, UI, operational, diagnostic, and observability state representation
text: The representation MUST NOT be treated as protocol state merely because it describes, realizes, stores, or observes protocol activity.
The authorization MUST identify the bounded pre-transition protocol state `Q0` against which `U` is authorized.

scope: Every implementation realizing an authorized transition
text: The implementation MUST NOT select, reconstruct, repair, or substitute a preferred pre-transition protocol state after authorization.
`Q1` MUST be derived only from the authorized `U`, governing `T`, applicable `Q0`, and complete published transition semantics.

scope: Every Protocol State Transition included as a committed state change in authoritative protocol-state history
text: The transition MUST have validly committed.

text: Partial execution or partial state change MUST NOT be included as committed history.

scope: Every operational attempt, diagnostic, retry, log, database row, event, report, error, cache record, or observability record

scope: Every history identifier, entry, representation, ordering record, diagnostic, log, field, route, test, example, serialization, storage key, and observability surface
text: A protocol-state history surface MUST NOT identify the Private Actor, introduce reusable participant identity, create cross-action linkage, or create an actor-reconstruction bridge.

The consequence MUST remain bounded to the published protocol meaning of the committed state change.

scope: Every relationship between a Published Result and a public protocol-state consequence
text: The interface-level Published Result and committed protocol-state consequence MUST remain distinct semantic roles.

scope: Every relationship between a Protocol Action Determination and a public protocol-state consequence
text: The Determination and committed consequence MUST remain distinct, including where both are publicly observable.

scope: Every relationship between authoritative successor state and public protocol-state consequence
text: The successor-state representation and its bounded public consequence MUST remain distinct without introducing an intermediate consequence object.

scope: Every public protocol-state consequence and every interpretation of it
text: The consequence MUST NOT be represented as application, factual, legal, social, institutional, user-intent, or off-protocol truth.

scope: Every public consequence identifier, representation, diagnostic, log, field, route, test, example, serialization, storage key, and observability surface

text: The recorded property MUST NOT be extended into actor identification, enrollment or admission provenance, hidden intent, or additional correlation meaning.

text: The classification MUST identify the actual bounded lifecycle stage and condition that occurred.

Rejection MUST remain the rejecting classification of one valid Determination produced by one completed Evaluation.
